utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I had thought I'd finished yesterday. On review, there was one particular small point that I should have put in terms, it being part of the case against this accused, and it arises from a document we've already looked at and that would take a couple of minutes. I was also provided last night, as a result of publicity given to the testimony of this witness, with two documents clearly of importance, documents that undoubtedly should have been provided to us pursuant to requests for assistance, assuming the documents are what they appear to be, and I would, with leave, ask questions about those two documents. It won't take very long but they are on a central issue dealt with by the witness yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Nice, but before you do that there's a matter that I have to raise with you. It has to do with the video recording that was played last Wednesday, the 1st. That was done with the Chamber's approval, but nonetheless it was in breach of an order issued by this Chamber on the 11th of May granting protective measures. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm grateful for advance warning of this problem which we were provided with, and I've been able to review the history. If there was any violation of the order, it was of course accidental and unknowing. I say "if there was a violation of the order" for this reason: The order was directed to the Defence, not to the Prosecution, and was limited in the relief it gave compared with what was sought. But in any event, because the issue wasn't conscious one way or the other, that may be a technicality. The position is that the team dealing with this case made all appropriate inquiries of both investigators and lawyers in the other case and was not alerted to the existence of any then existing restriction on use of the video at all. That may be because, of course, the need for protection had by then completely passed. The need for protection relied on by the Prosecution in its application in the other case related to a particular individual, and the concerns for that individual were then already matters of history. Had it not been, it wouldn't have been possible to rely on the video at all. So that inquiries were made; the existence of this order did not come to our attention. In those circumstances, what was done was done without knowledge of any potential breach or violation. In any event, it may be that technically there is no violation because the order was directed to the Defence and not the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: In any event, the Chamber issued an order yesterday which you must have seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: In which we indicated that in light of the widespread publicity, the Chamber was minded to lift the restrictions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: There is absolutely no resistance to that order by either those prosecuting this particular accused or indeed by anybody else in the office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Higgins.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the view of the assigned counsel is that it accords with the view taken by the Trial Chamber in this matter, given the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well. We'll issue an order lifting the restrictions. Mr. Nice, proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Mr. Stevanovic, just two points I'm going to raise with you this morning unless, of course, you've got answers to any of your queries, but that will come later. Dealing with the Skorpions and their engagement in Kosovo and in respect of the Cvjetan prosecution of which we spoke yesterday, you said this in evidence: "I claim that these two men -" that's the two accused - "belonged to the reserve force of the special anti-terrorist unit and they could not have belonged to any kind of paramilitary group. They were only as individuals members of the reserve force of that unit." Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that's roughly what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I want you to look at two documents that I'm going to suggest to you show beyond any doubt that the Skorpions were formally subordinated at the time of the Kosovo conflict, documents that came to light yesterday as a result of publicity given to your testimony and the subject of draft translations, and formal translations will be provided in due course. If you'd be good enough, please, to look first at the document that is headed "Republic of Serbia, Ministry of Internal Affairs, Organised Crime Directorate, O, Strictly Confidential." And if you will turn, please, to the second page in the Serbian version you will have, you will see that it is signed by Radovan Knezevic. You know who he was?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And I'm going to have to read most of this. It reads as follows: It's addressed to the Prokuplje court, so that's the court where these men were being tried. It says that: "The Organised Crime Directorate acted upon your request in regard to collecting needed information, for the purpose of conducting a successful investigation against ... Cvjetan Sasa and Demirovic Dejan..." Next point: "... established the following: The accused -" and they're named - "were members of the 'Skorpions' unit during March 1999. "The unit 'Skorpions' was founded as a unit of volunteers and had 128 members. "The commander of the unit 'Skorpions' was Slobodan Medic, also known as 'Boca', and his Deputy was Manojlovic Srdjan, also known as 'Srle'. "From the members of 'Skorpions' the following members have been identified by their nickname: Vuksic Zoran, also known as 'Zuca'; Djukic Zeljko, also known as 'Brka'; Medic Dragan, also known as 'Guljo'. "On 25 March 1999, the 'Skorpions' unit was transferred to the reserve formations of SAJ MUP, with the agreement of Colonel-General Vlastimir Djordjevic, the head of the Public Security Department of MUP at that time, and it was sent to Prolom Banja for further engagement. "On 27 March 1999, around 1800, Simovic Zoran, the commander of SAJ Beograd at that time, went to Prolom Banja in order to take the unit 'Skorpions' under his command. "Upon the arrival in Podujevo, Simovic and Medic went to the premises where SAJ was accommodated and they found there Stalevic Radoslav, the commander of the Pristina SAJ at that time. "Medic remained at the premises where SAJ was accommodated and Simovic and Stalevic went to OUP Podujevo, for consultations on further engagement and on accommodation of the members of the reserve formations of the SAJ - the unit 'Skorpions.' "During their stay in OUP Podujevo, Simovic and Stalevic heard several long firearms sounds from the direction of the location where the unit was to be accommodated. "Upon his arrival at the place of the incident, Simovic was informed that several members of the reserve formations of SAJ, the 'Skorpions' shot at women and children, the inhabitants of Podujevo. "From the active formation of SAJ the first person who arrived at the place of the incident was Vucelic Spasoje, also known as 'Vuk', who was at the time the commander of the platoon for support of SAJ, and currently deputy commander of SAJ MUP. "The first aid to the wounded ..." was dealt with. "After this event, Simovic gave orders to Medic to bring back all members of his unit under his command from Podujevo to Prolom Banja, which Medic did." Now, that's the first document. I suggest to you that that document makes it as clear as can be that the Skorpions were entirely formally subordinated to the SAJ of which you were at that time the commander.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me first answer the second part of the question. Never in my life have I been commander of SAJ nor have I ever been responsible for them. I only had contacts with the SAJ if I directly conducted training with them. But of course if this text is correct, it confirms the first part of your statement, but I am seeing this document for the first time, and I'm coming face-to-face with these facts for the first time. I told you yesterday what I found out from the newspapers, and I brought the newspapers because I thought it was my duty, and whenever you wish me to I'll show them to both you and the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I accept your first point. It's my error. They were subordinated to the public service part of the MUP of which you were a senior officer. The SAJ in particular were commanded by Zivko Trajkovic. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. The commander was Zivko Trajkovic, but I would add that concerning the other facts I presented yesterday, I still maintain they are true. Regarding the procedure for admission into the reserve force, and as to what I said that --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- admitting any units as such from any other category or structure is something not envisaged by the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... briefly and has one missing passage in it. That can be distributed. It's already been distributed, I think. And this comes -- goes to the assistant minister of public security, Djordjevic, and is signed indeed by the commander Zivko Trajkovic, and I'll read the first three and the last four shorter paragraphs. This document subject to the report of engagement of reserve formations for the need of the SAJ says this: "During the year 1998, the number of the members of special anti-terrorist units of MUP of Republic of Serbia significantly decreased because of the number of wounded and because of the transfer of SAJ Novi Sad to the State Security Department. "Because of these reasons, it was necessary to strengthen SAJ with a certain number of reservists for the purpose of conducting combat activities against Siptar terrorists. "With agreement of the head of the Public Security Department and the headquarters of MUP in Pristina, 128 members of the reserve formations were engaged, who were put on the list of the reserve formations of SAJ. These members were led by Medic Slobodan, with whom the members of SAJ had been fulfilling certain tasks on the territory of Slavonija, Baranja, and Western Srem. "The reservists were activated on the 25th of March, 1999. They were given the uniforms of PJP and the formation long arms from the Police Directorate of MUP. They were accommodated in the hotel in Prolom Banja where they were supported by SUP Prokuplje. The reservists did not leave the premises of their accommodation until 28 March 1999." The photocopy we have received, and we can see it in the original, would appear then to have a part of a sentence missing. I needn't read the long sentence. If the Court would turn to -- the long paragraph -- the second sheet, and if you please would turn to the fifth short paragraph from the end, which is still on the first page, I pick it up in this way: "Upon his return from Podujevo, the reserve formations remained there until 8th of April when they were sent back to Novi Sad, i.e., to Sremska Mitrovica. "Apart from the engagement on the 28th of March 1999, these members of the reserve formations were not engaged. They remained in the hotel in Prolom Banja and none of them left the accommodation premises, nor entered the territory of Kosovo. "During their stay in Prolom Banja, Colonel-General Pavkovic visited, met with the members of the reserve formations, and talked to Slobodan Medic. "Again, the need arose for the activating reserve formations, and on the proposal of Zivko Trajkovic, the commander of SAJ, and with the agreement of the headquarters in Pristina and the head of the department, 108 members of the reserve formations, led by Medic Slobodan, were re-engaged. "The members of the reserve formations came on the 26th of April, 1999, in the area of accommodation of SAJ in Kosovo Polje and immediately got involved in search of the territory and in the fight against the terrorists in the sector Jezero Mount, under the SAJ command and together with other active members of region. Their engagement lasted until the 9th of May, 1500 hours, when they returned to their places of living. They are still included in the list of reserve formations and worked exclusively under the command of the SAJ." That, then, from the commander. This document makes it absolutely clear, as Mrgud told us in evidence and as I suggested to you yesterday, that they were engaged, they were withdrawn after the incident involving Cvjetan, and they were re-engaged, all under the SAJ. Do you challenge that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I challenged that all day yesterday because I had no information whatsoever about the facts presented in this text. Now I see that these two documents were signed by people, two people whom I know personally, and I do not doubt that they presented correct facts here. The signatories of these two documents probably don't know, however, that a unit as such cannot be transferred into the reserve force. What the law envisages is that an individual can be accepted into the reserve force according to the procedure prescribed by law. Another pertinent fact is that if a decision had been made at all to admit a whole unit, which of course was not envisaged by the law, that decision could not have been made by the head of department. That would have had to be a decision of the minister, and that is something we don't see here. And that is my opinion, of course, not an assertion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stevanovic, is that perhaps not a reason why in the third paragraph of that last letter mention is made of 128 members of the reserve formations being engaged, and then in the last -- second last paragraph 108 members of the reserve formations were re-engaged, so that the individuals were engaged, in accordance with the law to satisfy the provision that you are talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, engagement on a particular task is one thing, but the previous question was recruiting the reserve force to belong to the police force. Recruiting reservists in 20 police unit is stipulated by law, and it's done at a lower-level unit, whereas the engagement of a reserve force for a particular assignment, mobilisation, conditionally speaking, is really up to the head of the actual service. The text or, rather, the first part of the quotation you referred to, the formulation is right. Members of the reserve force. It doesn't say the reserve unit of the police or a reserve unit of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honours, in view of the amount of time I've already taken, I'm not going to discuss this matter more with this witness but there is one point I want to put to him, and only one.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You understand, Mr. Stevanovic, that I don't accept that -- I'm suggesting to you that you have complete knowledge of all these things at the time. And if we look at this last document, we see that reservists were given uniforms of the PJP. You may not have been in charge of the SAJ, but you were indeed the commander of the PJP at the time, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not commander of the PJP at that time. I said that several times. Indeed it can be seen that they received PJP uniforms. However, PJP uniforms are a technical issue. Of course you can see that the police administration handed this out, but I was assistant minister whose line of work included the police, but in spite of all of these facts, I assert that I'm not aware of any of these facts highlighted here except for those that I referred to yesterday, namely that I knew that they carried out a crime, that they were returned the very instant and that a criminal report was filed, and I knew that later they were arrested or, rather, detained and brought before the relevant judicial organs. Those were the facts that I was aware of. As for the other facts contained in this document, I really was not aware of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Stevanovic, just so that I'm left in no doubt about this, the PJP fell somewhere under your responsibility; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The PJP was an independent, ad hoc unit, or, rather, in the plural, several units, within the public security sector. It was the police administration that carried out administrative work for the PJP, and among other things, I was in charge of the police administration as assistant minister.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And does the same arrangement or did the same arrangement apply in relation to the SAJ?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. The SAJ was not under my jurisdiction. It was not linked to the police administration. They were a permanent standing unit within the public security sector.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And yet it does appear from these documents that they fell within the province of the responsibility of Djordjevic, who was or is described, I think, here, as the head of the public security department of the police.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: However, the date and the context under which this letter is written is not clear upon its face, and usually a commander will send this kind of letter or report to the minister and it will be copied to assistant minister. So if you could tell how or why it was addressed to the assistant minister. Was it because he was head of the public sector?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely due to that fact, that this specific assistant minister is at the same time the head of the sector, the public security sector. However, that does not mean that the same letter was not sent to the minister, although I'm not sure about that, of course. I can only assume that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Were you aware at the time --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Nice, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Were you aware at the time of the Cvjetan court proceedings of Djordjevic preparing materials to forward to the court?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You know that you're described as being in charge -- for example, in something like "Under Orders" you're described as being the officer in command of the regular police throughout Kosovo at the time. Is that an incorrect description of your real role?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not a correct description of my real role. I already referred to my real role, and I wish I knew whose description this was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Again, for the sake of clarification, could you remind me of your relationship at the time, that's 1999 I think is the crucial part here, the first half of 1999, your relationship in the hierarchy with Djordjevic. I understood you to be in equivalent positions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct. Both of us were assistant ministers. And at the time, we were directly responsible to the minister. Of course he had broader responsibility than I did because he was in charge of the entire public security sector as head of the public security sector.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So when Djordjevic is described by Trajkovic as the head of the public security department -- no. He's not so described, is he? The impression --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He should say that. We can see from the heading that this was sent to the assistant minister, head of the public security sector. That's what it says in the address of this document. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is that not a description that can also be given to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No. I was not head of the sector. I was one of the three assistant ministers who were not heads of sectors. There is only one single head of the public security sector.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Who do you say was in charge of the public security in Kosovo in the first half of 1999?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've already explained that the system of command and control in the police in Kosovo and Metohija was that of peacetime, with the exception of the fact that the MUP staff was established to combat terrorism. And also, units were seconded to help the units in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Please, just help me if you can. If you can't, we'll move on to my last question on another topic. Which person was in charge of the public security police in Kosovo in the first half of 1999?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is not a person who had separate powers in terms of the functioning of the police in Kosovo. It's the minister. It's the head of the secretariat -- the heads of secretariats and the head of the sector, and parallel to that, the head of the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you were in charge, and your suggestion that you didn't know who Medic was and you didn't know about this investigation is, I would suggest, absolutely ridiculous. That's my suggestion to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Mr. Nort.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is not correct, Mr. Prosecutor, rest assured, and the investigation will prove that. The investigation in Belgrade is very intensive, and you will be assured that that will be proven and it will be proven that I have spoken the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honours, we will, of course, pursue by our request for assistance these documents and anything else associated with them given the somewhat central issue on which they now touch -- which they now touch. My last outstanding issue that I meant to raise relates to the diary at page 106. It's a very small point. The -- not a small point. It may be an important point but it's a point that I must put to this witness. If the Court -- it's Exhibit 404. The witness has the original before him. The Court will probably remember the entry, it's the "no corpse, no crime" entry where the word at the top -- Exhibit 440, I'm sorry if I gave the wrong number, which has at the top the words "president." The witness told us that this was something that happened in the presence of one president who, he offered, either this accused or Milutinovic. 440, page 106. The no corpse, no crime meeting, the word "president" at the top, the witness's evidence that it was either this accused or Milutinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: He said possibly this accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And I must make it quite clear to you, Mr. Stevanovic, the following: This document and your evidence reveals beyond any doubt, in my suggestion to you, that it was this accused at whose meeting you took these notes, and that you know that. What's your answer to that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already answered that that is what most probably happened. I cannot claim with 100 per cent certainty now who the president, without any name or surname, is, but I said that it is most probably the president of the FRY, Mr. Slobodan Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You have, I'm going to suggest to you, throughout your testimony said everything you possibly can to help this accused and if there was anyway you could respectably urge that this was another president --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Very well. I've made my point. I needn't repeat it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Unless there is answers to the questions that the witness took away with him about the documents, that's all I have to ask him. If he comes back with answers to those it might be that I would seek leave to ask him questions, but that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: May I just inquire, Mr. Stevanovic, have you received any answers yet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have received unofficial answers from the persons that I communicated with. These answers or, rather, this verification, which has not been completed yet, confirms what I said, that 11 persons from three documents were never employed by the Ministry of the Interior. As for an official answer, I have been instructed to address the National Committee for Cooperation with the Tribunal and the legally prescribed procedure. Obviously I overestimated my possibilities, and I overlooked the legal procedure envisaged by law, and for that I apologise to the Court. But it has been established that those persons were never employed by the Ministry of the Interior. I have unofficial corroboration of that. When I return, as any citizen, I will apply to receive such an answer officially. That is what my knowledge is for the time being, unofficially. Of course, the Prosecution can do that as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: By what means did you receive the answers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I telephoned some people at lower levels, and I know that they follow people, members of units and so on. No one could confirm to me that these persons were ever members of the Ministry of the Interior. Of course, this check was not complete, but I expect that through official procedure this can be confirmed officially as well. The newspapers are here. I shall submit them to the Registry and you will see for yourselves that what I said yesterday at the outset of the session was true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll return to that if necessary. Mr. Milosevic to re-examine, and you must endeavour, Mr. Milosevic, not to ask leading questions. Questions beginning with "Is it clear that..." "Is it logical that..." and so on, unless ingeniously phrased, are bound to be leading questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stevanovic, yesterday, let's first deal with this, Mr. Nice put a few questions to you in relation to Racak.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday -- or, rather, in the exhibits there are a great many documents that have to deal with Racak.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Not only now when you were preparing for this testimony, when these documents were compiled, but even at the time when you were in Kosovo and Metohija or in Belgrade, as assistant minister and as a general of the police, did you have occasion to familiarise yourself with a large number of these documents?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did familiarise myself with many documents, especially the circumstances involved in these events that were compiled by a particular working group. I'm not sure that I actually saw every operative information, Official Note, and the like.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right, General. No one expects you --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: -- to be familiar with each and every detail of each and every particular case. But now when you had a compilation of these documents before you - as you know, they are contained in several of these big binders - did you have occasion to look through all of them?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I looked at all the documents. Everything I read in the documents fits into what I know from before about Racak.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, all these documents that are contained here in the binders that have to do with Racak, are they official documents of the police and of the judicial organs or, rather, official documents related to what happened in Racak?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: There is no secondhand information there or rumour. These are only official documents that were presented?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. Official police and court documents. There are no newspaper articles, opinions of various persons, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. General, from these documents that we presented here in part, was it quite certain that in Racak there was a KLA unit?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was beyond dispute.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: From the documents and notes and collected information contained in these documents before the 15th of January, 1999, when there was a clash between the police and terrorists in Racak, was it established that in Racak there was a KLA unit?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, you're falling into error already and on an issue that is controversial. You can't lead on that. "Was it established in Racak that there was a KLA unit?"

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: For this passage of the evidence, I'd urge the Court to have in mind, in ruling on the accused's questions, the level of ignorance of the documents that it was established lay in the witness yesterday. He had -- he was given many opportunities to identify documents on particular topics and he declined every invitation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So, Mr. Milosevic, reformulate or move on to another issue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, I asked the witness quite unequivocally whether he looked through all the documents that are here, and there are a great many of them. The witness cannot be expected to know them all by heart. I asked him whether he reviewed all the documents that were presented here in relation to Racak, and his answer was affirmative. I assume that there is nothing leading about that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, but you have said in the last question, "Was it established in Racak that there was a KLA unit," and that is certainly leading.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. Robinson. I shall rephrase that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: During the examination-in-chief, General, did we have on the table and did you see documents that were created before the event in Racak and that refer to a terrorist group in Racak?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I saw these documents. I can also add that I had knowledge and information about that, that the group of Racak is constantly threatening the Stimlje-Dulje road on the road between Pristina and Prizren and the road to Urosevac. The key problem was on this regional road between Pristina-Prizren, and the Crnoljevo pass was under threat all the time, and there were a lot of casualties among the police and the army. All estimates showed that the group came from Racak and from surrounding villages whose names I cannot recall now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, did we have a document here, a press release of the Ministry of the Interior from that particular day, the 15th of January? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do remember that. There was a press release.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What did it say?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, it said that an anti-terrorist action was carried out in connection with the activity of that group, and the consequences of the activity of that group that were reflected in at least one killed policeman just before that event. I think it was the 10th of January, that that was the date referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did it say anything about the Verification Mission of the OSCE in that press release of the 15th?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It said that as regards that police activity, the Verification Mission was informed or they were present, I'm not quite sure now. I remember that the picture I saw was there too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, you say that you also remember the images showing?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The presence of the verifiers on the spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On the spot in Racak. Mr. Nice put some questions to you that had to do with your knowledge in this regard, that these were terrorists. Did you have an opportunity to listen to the testimony of their commander, Sukri Buja, who testified here?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I remember, but I do not recall any details. I remember that I think he said that he opened fire, that gunfire was opened from a heavy machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Precisely. Your memory serves you well. Buja Sukri also confirmed that fire was opened at the police, from a heavy machine-gun at that. In the documents from the on-site investigation, could you see that a great many trenches were dug and also that there were other things done that indicated that there had been fighting there?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the images at the time of the on-site investigation, it was quite clear --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: As the Court will understand, I'm only two happy for the accused to use as much time as he can given the percentage that I have to achieve, but does this arise in any way from cross-examination? And if it doesn't, should it be permitted or should it be stopped? It's a matter for the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if we are going to look at it that way, then it's quite clear that an enormous number of questions put by Mr. Nice does not arise from the examination-in-chief at all, and yet you did not interrupt him. In addition to that, you could have noticed that Mr. Nice often made statements, and you never interrupted him. I don't know why you make this kind of selection and why you have a completely different attitude to the questions that I'm putting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I reject that suggestion of any kind of selection on the part of the Trial Chamber. The Trial Chamber has dealt with you fairly. I'm going to allow you to put the question at this time. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can just continue with my answer. From the pictures, you could see that in the area around Racak and surrounding hills that there were a lot of -- there was a lot of fortification that had been prepared by KLA members, and at the on-site investigation we could see that the on-site investigation team and the policemen providing security were shot at. They opened fire. That's what I saw on the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, Mr. Nice showed you some photographs. Do you have any idea who took those photographs?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And that's why I asked the Prosecutor, and if I understood him correctly, he said that it was international organisations. Perhaps I'm not remembering it correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, do you know when the photographs were taken?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether a single photograph of those photographs was taken on the day the event occurred or whether they were taken later on?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know anything about that, when the photographs were taken or anything like that, or who took them, for that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you know whether anybody was able to take photographs on the day the event occurred?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all I know is that it was a day when the police, after the operation, did not have control over the area, and all I can do is to assume who could have taken those photographs, given the period of time, that is to say after the operation started up until the police was withdrawn from the region of Racak.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, in the documents that were presented here, is there evidence and proof of the fact that a paraffin glove test was taken and that orders were issued for the paraffin glove test to be taken which was supposed to show whether anybody shot --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, you cannot ask the question in that way, "Is there evidence and proof that a paraffin glove test was taken?" I mean, that is virtually putting the answer into the witness's mouth.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's a generally known fact, Mr. Robinson, and Mr. Nice tried once again to explain something along the lines of the fact that civilians were killed there, and even the sparrows know today that it was a clash between the KLA and the police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, did you cross-examine on the paraffin glove test?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm not allowing that. It doesn't arise. Move on to another question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in the cross-examination, Mr. Robinson, he asked the witness whether --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I've stopped you. I've already ruled. Move on to another question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear the testimony of Adam Bo, the German journalist who investigated how a boy was killed?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I did, yes. I think so. And if I remember correctly, there was a break in some sort of hedge and something along those lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, that is what it was about, but did his testimony indicate that there was fighting there or that there was killing of civilians?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I would hate to think that you are being deliberately mischievous and in breach of the Rules of the Court, because if you are, the Trial Chamber will take certain steps. If you cannot conduct the re-examination in conformity with the Rules of the Court, in particular with relation to leading questions, the re-examination will be terminated, and I must make that very clear, because practically every question you're asking is in breach of the Rules. The witness must give his testimony, give his evidence unaided, unaided by you, and that's the purpose of the rule prohibiting leading questions in examination-in-chief and in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I add one point? Reassuring though it is to hear how good the witness's recollection is of the evidence he's reviewed, he's not here to comment on evidence that others have given earlier, and that's one of the various things the witness is trying to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Proceed, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, as a high-ranking officer of the police force who, as you said a moment ago yourself, had at his disposal these documents here having to do with Racak, is the conclusion that you draw from all the material facts of what you learnt from the documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm stopping that. "Is the conclusion you draw..." that is going to end up as a leading question. You may ask him what is the conclusion that he draws, but you're not to tell him the conclusion. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that's just what I was going to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That was not indicated by the way you formulated the question at all, Mr. Milosevic. You're being very insincere. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, take a look at how I started asking the questions in Serbian and then you'll see whether I'm sincere or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, General, tell me, in view of the fact that you were at a high-ranking position in MUP and you looked at all this information and went through it, what conclusion did you draw about the events in Racak, about that particular event on the 15th of January, 1999, in Racak?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the conclusion can be reduced to several theses. In Racak, the police was attacked by terrorists while they were doing -- going about their lawful duty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I interrupt there, and can you tell me, what is the basis for that statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The basis for that statement is all Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the information that I have, both orally immediately after the event, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you have a statement from any police officer to the effect that that's what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not have a statement by a policeman, but I do have a report about the entire event, and it is to be found in the documents that are to be found here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Proceed, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did the police, General, have any knowledge at all about the killing of civilians in Racak?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in that operation itself, but it did have knowledge about killings, including civilians and, of course, policemen and soldiers on the roads which are very close to Racak.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, had the police killed anybody there, would proceedings be taken as provided for by the laws and provisions of our country?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry, I don't understand that. I thought the police killed 40 people. So what proceedings were taken by the laws and provisions of your country to investigate that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, let me say there's a terminological programme [as interpreted]. The police did not kill. If you use the word "kill," it means kill with intent, premeditated killing, whereas the police applied force to which it has right to, and the consequence of that force being applied was the death of these individuals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That is not my understanding of the word "kill" in English. It may be a different situation in B/C/S, but kill is kill. You can kill someone accidentally, you can kill them deliberately, you can kill them negligently, you can kill them in all sorts of ways, but killing means destroying life in English. Is it different in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Serbian, and as I understand it, they are different things. Somebody can lose his life as the consequence of a killing, or it can be the result of the legitimate use of force. So in Serbian there are some differences. I apologise if there are not in English. Perhaps I wasn't clear enough. And let me add with -- in a response to your question, I read a report which was compiled by a working group which had the task of investigating the circumstances surrounding the event and to draw conclusions from that. I have said, I think on two occasions, that I assume that there are statements by leaders and individuals who took part in that operation, however, I do not have them here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do we have the working group report here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think we quoted it in answer to one of the questions that was asked. We quoted the conclusions from a report by that particular group, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Working group, a working group. All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, in view of the fact that you are an educated man in your profession, do you know that casualties in war conflicts between the armed formations of two sides is qualified as killing or the result of a war conflict?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was the sense of my response to the Judge a moment ago. In our language, killing is either within intent or chance, and -- and manslaughter. And of course the consequences of war effects are not considered to be killings when loss of life is incurred in wartime.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let us make an assumption. I don't want to ask a leading question. The conflict between a police unit and a terrorist group, for instance, from which -- which leads to death, death of a number of individuals, can it be considered, according to any provisions or anything, as killing?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can as an excess if there was intentional killing of anybody outside the provisions provided for by law governing the use of firearms, but the killing of terrorists in a clash between police and terrorists in principle cannot be considered as murder.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. We won't deal with this question of Racak any more except for one more. Let me ask one more question. Does a single document which is provided in these two binders about Racak, are they documents which did not emanate from the regular work of the Ministry of the Interior or the Judiciary?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not seen any other document, any document outside those two categories of documents that you just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well, General. Now let's deal with your diary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, which of the tabs is the working group report?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bonomy, I'll try and find it during the break. There are many exhibits, but I can't tell you just off the top of my head now, and I'll ask one of my associates to look through the documents and try and come up with that and I'll hand it over to you after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, we're now going to deal with your diary. Mr. Nice calls this a diary. Have you got it in front of you?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, no, I do not. I haven't got it among my documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, you ought to have it.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't managed to find it. Which tab is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It's tab 17 -- or, rather, binder 17, tab 440.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nice says that this is some sort of diary of yours. Is it a diary or an agenda?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's not a diary. It's an agenda, a notebook in which I noted down certain theses, some of my own thoughts, some of other people's thoughts. There are, of course, some personal notes as well, quite apart from my job.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are we in private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, we are in public session.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm sorry about that. May the passage be redacted from public display, going right back to the beginning of that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We're ready to get the tab numbers now, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In connection with Racak, Mr. Bonomy asked for tab numbers related to the activities of the police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, the working group report. I don't want to be involved in a wild goose chase.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's very specific.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is a set of documents that begins with tab 395, which contains a plan of implementation of operative and tactical measures and investigative steps regarding the incident in Racak village, and it says on the last page the working group of the MUP, and three MUP officials --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Binder 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, continue, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, have you found tab 395?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Does this tab contain the plan for the implementation of operative and tactical measures and investigative steps drafted by the working group?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is the plan that we analysed to some extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Did this working group consist of high-ranking police officials?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We can see that from their signatures and names at the end of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: From the signatures, names, ranks, and titles, the positions they occupied. According to what you know, was this plan implemented, and is it the case that in these tabs 395, 396, 397 we find a clarification of the circumstances under which the crime of terrorism was perpetrated in Racak, Stimlje municipality?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is tab 396.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The chronology follows in tab 397. Is this an entire set of documents related to the event?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are the documents of this working group, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did these documents arise from a careful review of all the facts related to the event?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the high level of this working group should be a confirmation of very careful, professional and meticulous work in studying this incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is 397 signed by anyone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is precisely what I noticed just now. It seems the last page of the document is missing. This is the document I meant when in response to previous questions I mentioned a report of the working group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What about 396? Is it complete?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot claim one way or another, but it seems that it, too, is incomplete.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: 396 ends with the words "The following plan is hereby adopted," and then nothing follows.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct. That's correct. And from that I conclude that it is incomplete.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Should the plan be tab 395?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The plan is 395, and that one should be complete. It has the last page, and it has signatures, at least in my copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And who are the signatories?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in my copy, at the end it says MUP working group, head of department of criminal investigation police, Major General Dragan Ilic; and then head of department in the public security sector, Mioljub Nikolic; and head of the forensic and technical centre, Vladimir Aleksic. And you can see copies of their signatures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We have the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, we were in private session. Had you finished your questioning for the private session? If not -- if you have, then we can remain in public session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I think we can remain in public session. We will now go back to this agenda of General Stevanovic. However, before I do that, I wish to draw your attention again to tab 400, which follows these 5, 6, and 7, and it contains the press release by the Ministry of the Interior on the 15th of January, 1999, saying that measures were taken concerning Racak and that the Kosovo Verification Mission of the OSCE was informed about the measures. This is dated the 15th of January, 1999. It doesn't say yet what had happened. It just says that measures were taken and notified to the KVM. It indicates that the measures taken were related to the terrorist group that was active there and that they were notified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Move on to your next area of re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, this agenda of yours, does it represent your notes which you could have in any case made available to anyone who was interested in events and activities related to your work from that time?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let me not ask only general questions. I'll ask only one: Do these notes contain anything that in your opinion is not consistent with our regulations, that in any way casts doubt on the regularity of policework and the state authorities in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am certain that there is nothing of the kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. We will now go through some of these quotations. I have no time to deal with the entire agenda, but let us just gain a general picture from these notes of yours. Please turn the page ending with numbers 380. That's the ERN number. These are the only numbers I think that are in sequence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Give us the English number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, the English number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Or the date.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, unfortunately -- let me just see.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may assist.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 8th February, 1999. Have you found this ERN number 0172380? On this page there is a date. That's the 8th February, 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It says in the first, second, third -- eighth line, eighth line, "Repair" or "improve the national -- the ethnic structure of the police force in Kosovo." That's your handwriting; would you read it.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you -- you mean where it says "reserve force"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What's the first -- I see. 22?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't understand. What are you asking me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see "Correct the multi-ethnic composition of the police in --" et cetera. Is that what you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This sentence in the original says: "Correct, or rectify, the multi-ethnic composition of the police in NP -" it's probably Novi Pazar - "Kosovo and Metohija and SU," and that certainly means Subotica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. What is the point of this note which you used as your own reminder?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had, conditionally speaking, a certain problem with an unfavourable ethnic composition of the police force in Kosovo and Metohija, in the SUP of Novi Pazar, and in the SUP of Subotica, so our objective was to improve the ethnic composition of the police force in the sense of including more Albanians, Muslims, and Hungarians.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So that is a commitment of your force.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The strategic commitment of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Turn the next page, the 9th February, 1999. It says "The federal government."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It says "Session for the Commission of Cooperation with the OSCE."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what does it relate to? It says: "Racak corpses." What was it about?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is obviously a matter for that session. I probably attended it and they discussed Racak and the incidents in Racak, but I could not assert with any certainty in more specific terms what the subject of discussion was. It was the 9th of February. It was probably believed even then that the issue of Racak was topical.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But this was a session of the Commission for Cooperation with the OSCE?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On the next page on the same sheet, without any date but it is typed as the next page, it says: "Focus on." Will you read this, the writing that follows. You will find it more easily, it's your handwriting.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says: "Focus on: Protection of roads, facilities of special importance, settlements and facilities where Serbs gather." Second item: "Detection and arrest of perpetrators of terrorist acts."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Stop there, please. Was it the general task of the police, as you say here, to detect and deprive of freedom perpetrators of terrorist acts, or to kill them?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this note here confirms what I repeated several times already: Not killing but detecting and depriving of freedom perpetrators of terrorist acts. That's what is written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What are these pivotal tasks?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Planning intervention directed at certain hotbeds, including preparations for building obstacles on axes of entry of the military component, probably ground component, on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What was meant here was probably the possibility of aggression by ground forces.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. And the last bullet is "Implementation of all measures related to the OSCE," and it is slightly harder to make out what follows in the brackets.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Further on, when it says "Characteristics of terrorist activity."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: "Presence in certain parts of the territory and a fully tolerant attitude of the OSCE representatives."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says. It says: "Characteristics of terrorist activity are still: Additional organisation, equipping and arming." The second one is: "Presence in certain parts of the territory, with a fully tolerant attitude," probably "of representatives of the OSCE."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. And then "Other characteristics" you mention. More frequent acts of terrorism?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I say in inhabited areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: "Increased number of murders of members of the Albanian national community."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And then further on it speaks of the situation in police units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Does it say "Strength stands at 10.021"?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That's in line with the Clark-Naumann Agreement in Belgrade or, rather, Djordjevic-Byrnes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: When you move on to the next page, is the first sentence, "All obligations towards OSCE should be carried out"?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what's written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Does it say here: "In Paris the representatives of the Kosovo Albanians" -- I can't read this word -- "and in our -" something illegible - "are terrorists."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, here it says in Paris there are representatives of the Kosovo Albanians, and the rest, it's hard for me to read it. "Representatives of Kosovo Albanians" is under quotation marks, which would mean that they're terrorists or something like that. I'm not sure really.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then it says: "The army of Yugoslavia has to have deterrence activities."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is the usual primary objective when there is a threat of aggression.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Was that all in line with the measures that were taken then?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Was that a record of things said by someone else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Possibly, because in the heading it says "Probably Minic," or "Milic." I don't know who Milic could be, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Where it says "All obligations towards the OSCE should be carried out"?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Before that it probably says "Minic."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That item starts with the -- a note, you said, "Chaired by M. Milic." Second line from "federal government." Do you note it? February 9, it says "Federal government. Session of the Commission for Cooperation with the OSCE, chaired by M. Milic."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That's incorrect. It's probably Milomir Minic, because I do not know of a Milic. I simply don't know a person with that surname. Perhaps I have forgotten this very moment. But, of course it doesn't mean that all of the notes are his. These notes on the previous page are quite certainly mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, could you please move on ahead to 384, please, 384. It says the 11th of February, 1999.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: There's a lot of text there. It's very dense. I don't want to dwell on it very long. It would require a lot of time, though. On the right-hand side --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: -- it says: "Main attacks --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "Main tasks," interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then it says: "Protection of security of the republican citizens."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: "Combatting terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija is the topmost security and political task." Is that what it says here?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What's the next: "In the field of SK." What is SK?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Suzbijanje kriminaliteta," "crime control."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. You can make any abbreviations you like, I'm just asking you what that means. So it means in the area of crime control.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what is KD?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Criminal offences. Probably combatting crime. Criminal offences jeopardising the health, property, and lives of citizens. That's the first one. Should I read on?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, all right. It all pertains to curbing crime.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what is the last one here? "Combatting crime, attitude towards --"

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Injured parties." That was a very important thesis at that moment, to devote more attention to injured parties in any criminal offence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Further on it says: "In JRM." That is law and order?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, public law and order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: "Ensure normal life of the citizens and the normal functioning of the institutions of the system." And then it says: "In the field of traffic security, traffic safety." So are these normal, regular police tasks that were discussed? What meeting is this from?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this is from a meeting that I had at the SUP in Jagodina on the 11th of February, 1999. This is a meeting I held with the leaders of that municipal Secretariat of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was my reminder for that meeting. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: If you move one page ahead, you talk about improving efficiency in work.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Improving the level of legality in work. I wish to draw your attention to that, as well as the reputation of the service, conduct, and appearance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: One of these bullets says, in the middle of the page: "It is not important what we think about ourselves."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "We must always take care about what citizens think of us. We must always heed what citizens think of us." I wanted to say that it's not important if we perceive ourselves in a positive context. That doesn't matter. What matters is what citizens think of us and how they perceive us. I wanted to draw your attention to that domain pertaining to the relationship between the citizens and the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So this is your instructive meeting with --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The leaders of the SUP in Jagodina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Please look further on. 387 is the page. From the second --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What's the date for that one, Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says here the 11th of February, 1500 hours. "Analysis of work."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And now on the right-hand side you say: "In spite of a series of problems, there is an immeasurable contribution of the POL to the creation of conditions for bringing about a lasting solution --"

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Peaceful solution."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: "-- peaceful solution to problems in Kosovo and Metohija." And then you say: "Cannot be resolved by policework."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you say that problems should be resolved in a political manner. Is that the point of what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The policy of the ministry that we received through the minister, and that is that the fundamental way of resolving the crisis in Kosovo and Metohija is peacefully through democratic means, that the problem cannot be resolved by policework, and that the police only has the role of enabling the creation of minimal conditions for resolving problems through peaceful means.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. And then on the next page you talk about general primary tasks. It pertains to the same meeting, I assume, because there's no other date. There is nothing there. So it is general primary tasks; improving the overall efficiency of work in all lines of work?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Improving the level of legality in work, the reputation of the service, its appearance and conduct.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's similar to the previously mentioned theses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Then "Upgrading the objective level of responsibility of top personnel. Organise a systematic approach to all tasks. Looking to the future."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then you talk about primary line tasks, "the protection of security R and citizens." That's probably of the republic and citizens.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: "Suppressing terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija," and then the next bullet is "Crime prevention."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: "Public law and order." "Curbing or, rather, preventing criminal offences which directly threaten the lives, health, and property of citizens."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then "ensuring a normal life for the people and the functioning of institutions."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The functioning of institutions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What does it say here at the end of this page? "The police must through lawful work --" I cannot read this.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can. "The police must through lawful work --" oh, I'm sorry. "Returning inter-ethnic --" I can't read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: "Trust --"

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Trust and confidence," if I see it. So it's the role of the police in restituting inter-ethnic tolerance and confidence. That's the gist of it. I cannot read this but I remember those theses of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: When you look at the next page, in the fourth bullet you can see: "Through proper and lawful work the police should bring back inter-ethnic confidence," something along those lines; right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And on the left, it says: "Efficiency and lawfulness in every --" I cannot read this. "In all work"?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot find this. "Efficiency and lawfulness in work." But I don't know what kind of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then there is page 390. It ends with 390. That is the 14th of February at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should be a similar meeting but in Novi Pazar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: No. It's the senior staff meeting of the minister.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes. Yes, I can see it up here now. And then Novi Pazar is up, further up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It only says: "An analysis of work was carried out." And then on the 14th, it says: "The minister's collegium," or senior staff meeting.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then the members of the minister's collegium are mentioned here; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is there anybody outside the MUP who was present?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, what are you seeking to establish by this evidence?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'm seeking to establish, because these are personal notes from the work notebook of General Stevanovic, the extent to which these activities were really in line with state policy, as he also wrote it down here, and in keeping with lawful measures taken by the police in every way.
