Although Mr. Nice wishes to prove something different, we are going to deal with all of his quotations. May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. You're still remaining with the diary?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You're still remaining with the diary, or the agenda, as you call it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. This is an agenda. It's quite obvious. I already asked the general.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You say here the minister.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are supposed to be his theses, what follows.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. What does he say here? "We will do everything to resolve Kosovo and Metohija in a peaceful way."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what it says in the third bullet here, third asterisk.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: "However, if the country is attacked, we shall defend ourselves."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Regardless of how strong the enemy may be."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On the right-hand side, does it say this: "We have -- our orientation is a multi-ethnic Kosovo"?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says: "Our option is a multi-ethnic Kosovo."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Option, right. But it doesn't matter, it means the same. "Our option is a multi-ethnic Kosovo," it says. Right. "We must avoid a civil war." Is that what it says as well?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. And then something Mr. Nice went on to quote from that same meeting where it is established that everything should be solved peacefully, that our option was a multi-ethnic Kosovo, that we should avoid a civil war, and then it says: "Our enemies Kandic, Biserko," Mr. Nice quoted that. Why did that -- was that position circulated at the time amongst you?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That position -- well, I've already explained. It was there amongst us because of the fact that the organisation or organisations led by these ladies, as I've already said, were one-sided and biased, in our opinion, in presenting the facts, and we had quite different information as to what the facts were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: For example? Give us an example.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's difficult for me to remember specifically and quote an example, but I assume that it was a question of certain accusations with respect to some specific events, most probably, and in regard of that, the results of the investigation were quite different from them from what we found ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you're discussing that at the senior staff meeting, the collegium of ministers? You were able to speak amongst yourselves frankly, and you knew whether what you were talking about is correct or not?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was certainly correct, and I assume we can see that the minister stated so loud and clear here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On the following page -- I can't find the ERN number, but when you turn the page, 392 I believe is the ERN number. It's placed in different positions on the page so I'm not able to follow, but that seems to be the ERN number, 392 being the last digits. You say "For the minister's collegium." That's the heading; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It would mean that this is an aide-memoire for the collegium.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you were preparing for this senior staff meeting and writing down the basic points, the basic theses that you wished to set out.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Fine. And then you say that in UP, that is to say the plan of preparations for what should be taken with respect to a possible NATO aggression.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the UP means "Uprava policije," the police directorate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then it says: "From airstrikes to the entry of ground forces." Was it common knowledge that a ground aggression was expected?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was common knowledge, and it was always taken into account when making every assessment and contingency plans.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. Take a look at 394 now, please. ERN number 394, last digits. There is no date here, however, it does say: "Crime also a priority." Is that right? That's what the minister says. "Priority Kosovo and Metohija. Crime also a priority." Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's page 42.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now I'm going to skip over some of the following passages. Now, please, take a look at page 402, 172402. On the right-hand side, it says: "The police --" at the beginning of the page, on the right-hand side, it says: "The police in Kosovo and Metohija are fully observing the agreement on the OSCE mission." Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's under number 1, the first point.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What else does it say after that? Read it out, please.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The second thesis, it says: "In this regard, the police protects the security of the mission members."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page 51.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And then the second point: "Informs the mission about events and actions." Third point: "Enables the mission to move around without hindrance." And the fourth point: "Allows the mission to monitor the work of the police." Yes, that's right, "to monitor the work of the police."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then it goes on to say: "This does not, of course, mean that in individual cases the police does not make mistakes," because it says, "We're getting in general complaints."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "That, of course, does not mean that in individual cases the police does not make mistakes."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What does it say after that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Every case reported will be investigated in detail, the measures prescribed by law taken, and will inform --" I'm not quite sure what it says there. That's rather illegible. But anyway, I think it says "will inform the person filing the complaint." That's what it should mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what does it say after that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The event must be reported," probably to the district police station in the area. The time, place, description, the damage incurred, persons present, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. So that, then, is the end of February. Is that all in keeping with what you described about how the police works?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now look at page 408, please. Just briefly, on the left-hand side, it says here: "At a meeting of the ministers." It's the 1st of March. "Meeting with minister. The situation is becoming more complicated in Kosovo and Metohija. The opening of Kacanik, movement of civilians, violent conflicts." Does that, then, indicate the problems that are caused by the activities of the KLA or some other problems?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, quite obviously it refers to KLA activities. The opening of Kacanik. It cannot mean us opening Kacanik but that some problems are opening up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Of course. And what does this "movement of civilians" mean?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That the civilians are on the move, are moving. That's what that means. And that's the beginning of March, if this date is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. On page ERN 416, last digits, under number 1 on the left-hand side, it says: "A number of meetings to -- in support of the peaceful resolution of the Kosovo crisis --" I can't read the rest of that.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says, "without problems and against the aggression."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now take a look at page 419, ERN number. What does it say there? It's a meeting of the provisional Executive Council in Kosovo and Metohija. It says: "The police in case of an aggression on the Republic of Serbia will take the following steps." And what does it say?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. It says: "Intensify the struggle against terrorist forces in all their -" perhaps strongholds or something like that, a similar word.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. And then it says: "Intensify the protection of populated areas"; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And then it says -- the second point is to step up protection of the main roads.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So we're talking about stepping up protection of inhabited populated areas as being one of the police tasks; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, we're taking this one by one, in order, and we come to 421. I can't really see what the date is to which this refers. However, it says here on the left-hand side: "Prevent looting. Conduct toward civilians." Under 6, it says: "Movement of civilians." So in what sense is movement of civilians mentioned here?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the fact that it's a problem, that it's something that's taking place, happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then on the right-hand side you are quoting somebody as saying: "Now when we are the victims, we mustn't be criminals. We mustn't commit crimes."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I assume that I quoted that quotation as something that the minister said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So that's something the minister said, is it?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did he say that to draw attention to the people that everything must be done pursuant to the law, or in some other sense?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exclusively in that sense because we really did become the victims and we felt there might be some kind of retaliation and he insisted that nothing like that must be allowed to happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On the next page, 422, it says here: "Military courts urgent. Criminal reports for the detained. Announce the verdicts, the judgements."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think that was a position that I put forward at one point, but I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then it says: "Detailed clearing up of the battlefield."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Then it says: "Movement of civilians." Now, what does that mean, "movement of civilians" there; in what sense?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's always in the same sense. Whenever that is written, it means the problem of the movement of citizens.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. The next page, number 23. We have -- I can't quite read this, but it says something "towards Kacanik."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says: "Columns towards Kacanik."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right, fine. And then what does it say?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't make it out. I can't read what it says here. "Get the civilians away." I can't -- I can't read what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, what does it say after that? It says "From KM towards Montenegro," I assume.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that that refers to those same columns. From Kosovska Mitrovica is the KM.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Right, Kosovska Mitrovica. Fine. Now, on the next page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Staying there, staying there, after KM, it says: "Military police at the border turning them back," and you put a question mark there. Could you explain that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right. Well, we were thinking along those lines, and when I testified whether they should be allowed to go there or whether they should -- should be stopped from coming, or use force. That's what I said several times, whether force should be used to prevent them from leaving or to allow them to leave and thus get away from the war zone. And then of course it speaks about activities of stopping them, returning them, and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So did the police consider that returning them back is problematic at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, of course not. The police wanted and the army wanted them to stay where they were, but it was assessed that turning them back could be problematic for them and that the police could be held responsible if something happened to them; if they were bombed or if they fell casualty in any way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, on the next page, 424, you speak here on the right-hand side of a series of -- you have a series of points. It says "ATA." That's anti-terrorist activity, is it?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then you have "Law and order."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. Law and order for joint patrols, the patrols of the army and police. That's what is meant there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Then we have "Crime prevention."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what does it say in brackets?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't read it, it's not legible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then it says: "Protection of civilians - disarmament, disarming."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then it says clearing up the terrain - "asanacija" is the word used, of -- then we have court jurisdiction, then we have volunteers, then it says: "There are no volunteer units."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, could you explain that to us, please. What does this mean?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The concept of volunteers was frequently used mistakenly and was used to explain the reserve force. The reserve force. So I wrote down my thoughts on the subject there, that is to say that the concept and notion Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. used here implies the presence of groups who should not be in Kosovo. We cannot tolerate the presence of volunteer units in Kosovo. That's what that means.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Right. Fine. Now, please, could you comment 426, page 426 on the right-hand side. If you want to do so, you can give us more comments, but what it says at the end: "All police action. All police action in K and M."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "All police actions in K and M --" "All police operations in K and M were directed solely again the terrorists, not against the Albanians who are citizens on a footing of equality in their own state."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Fine. Now, on the following page, 427, it says: "For the meeting." Is that your preparation for the meeting?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably for a meeting. I can't actually see which particular meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But regardless of which meeting, what does it say here? "Preventing looting, stealing, and criminal offences, together with the Yugoslav army and independently."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Anybody can detain the perpetrator of a crime, of a criminal offence, and I've already said that in response to a question. Then it goes on to say: "Remand in detention for up to 30 days," and we mention wartime provisions in that regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, please, on the right-hand side there, at the end of the -- bottom right-hand side, there are different tasks and assignments that are enumerated, and then the Yugoslav army and arrests. It says: "Relations with the VJ and arrests." What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Joint patrols and all perpetrators of crimes to be apprehended. Everything that I've explained. We decided that the police can arrest a soldier if a soldier commits a crime, and the vice versa; the army can take into custody a policeman if a policeman commits a crime. And that is pursuant the Criminal Code; anybody can arrest the perpetrator of a crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right, and then at the bottom of that page, it says what "with the VTO"? That is to say how do you cooperate with military territorial bodies; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, VTO, military territory -- territorial organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And then what does it say? "Search for graves"?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. And searching for mines, anti-tank mines, infantry mines, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then what does it say?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Records of those killed, evacuation, and so on. Mass graves, it says. Rest periods for the personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: When did you jot that down, mass graves, in what sense?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To identify them and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On page 430, you say: "The protection of people and property, the basic work of the police." Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Basic task," it says, "basic tasks."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Ah, right, yes, basic tasks. Protection of people and property as a basic police task. And then on the left-hand side it says something, "Property, movement of civilians." What does that refer to? That is the 16th of April. There's a date there, 16th of April, 1999.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you help me out here; is that on the left-hand side?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the left-hand. It says, "vehicles, property, movement of civilians." You're quoting someone, I don't know who.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, if I read this right, what is cautioned against is wilful behaviour of civilians, the police, the military, et cetera, related to vehicles, property, blank certificates, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I had the impression that you were quoting someone because there's a colon there.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it says, "wilful behaviour."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. So why is wilful behaviour indicated here?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To have in mind that problem and to prevent it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So that is mid-April 1999. Next page, 431. That is the 22nd of April, 1999. Number 2, it says -- could you please read this.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Legality in conduct." It should probably be in conduct as such and measures taken, but that's it. Basically, the police is responsible for law and order and crime prevention, especially in populated areas. "We request increased engagement of the military police in suppressing wilful behaviour in crime by military personnel."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Could you please look at the next page.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What's this on the left-hand side, the slanted note? "Rodja"? It's pretty illegible here on my copy.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot read that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: "The men from Sid are coming in PJP uniforms."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, uniforms PJP.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Could Your Honour assist me with the page number? I haven't found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what does it say here?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The men from Sid are coming in PJP uniforms. Uniforms for local security." And I don't know what it says as the third line, the third bullet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What does it pertain to?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know what it is specifically. Probably that they were coming and bringing uniforms. "Unity," "Jedinstvo." It could be the Jedinstvo factory that makes uniforms. It's under quotation marks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now look at the right-hand side, please. The right-hand side seems quite interesting. It says: "From the very beginning," and it says so in block letters: "Treatment of civilians who are returning."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then what does it say underneath?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Army -- the army should say where it is not possible. We, too --"

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What is that? Could you please dwell on the first one. Does it mean where the military positions are they cannot -- they should say where they can and cannot?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the objective here is for the army to say which are the locations where they cannot return, to which they cannot return.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then what does it say: "We should provide them with protection"?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "We should provide them with protection provided that they hand in weapons, do not take in terrorists, do not hinder the movements of the police, assign local security." Those were the three theses for discussion with these civilians. Of course, protection was always guaranteed to them irrespective of these theses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what does it say under number 2: "Refugee columns"?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Refugee columns. Secure refugee columns. Discretionary checks of persons, vehicles, and cargo."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Going out over the border not en masse." "Not en masse," that's what it probably says. "Suspicious ones should be detained, processed, kept, arrested." It is a reference to persons who would be interspersed among the civilians and who are obviously suspects.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. That is the end of April. Were there less border crossings at that time?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Of course. That's my recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. If you look at the next page, it says: "Asanacija," under number 3, sanitisation. "Columns of refugees," and then "asanacija," sanitisation. What is OKP?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is departments of crime investigation in secretariats. And then in brackets, it says: "(Investigating judge, office of the prosecutor.)"

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In relation to sanitisation, activities are mentioned here of the departments of the -- of crime investigation, of investigating judges and prosecutors?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then it says, "Immediately after taking a territory," and then line.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That means that immediately after a territory is taken, the crime investigation department, the investigating judges and the prosecutors act on this, that is on sanitisation.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the meaning of that thesis. And then you can see further on, "Instructions of the investigating judge, burial, individual documentation," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What's the rest? "Refugee columns."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says, "Traces of refugee columns." I've already explained that. Abandoned vehicles, objects, roads that were blocked in that way, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. 4 is property. We'll skip over that. And what is 5? I cannot read 5, it's not legible enough for me.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Legality" is the heading.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. I couldn't read that word.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Ban on torchings, ban on violence against civilians --" and it's very hard to read the rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, on the next page there is a reference to volunteers. Please, let's see what this is all about and whether you can remember and whether you can assist with clarifying this. That is 434. On the left-hand side, number 14. It says: "Report, notes on," and then --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "On behaviour of volunteers." That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What kind of volunteers were they? Volunteers who established some kind of units or volunteers within?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it's the volunteers, then it's those who were within the army ranks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. And then on the next page, under number 1, you quote persons who were taking part in the discussion, I assume.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And it says?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Bogi," who is probably Janicijevic, and it says: "Problems with volunteers and wilfulness." That has to do with what was said earlier on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, the remark is identical, right, but at a different time?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at a different time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On the same page there is another reference to volunteers. Somebody else is speaking about that.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is somebody else who is talking it in the same sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: This person who was speaking says: "Torchings out of hand."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He is saying that he cannot put the problem under control.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then it says: "Local self-government."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In Kosovska Mitrovica is not functioning."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: There's no date here. What is the time frame? To which period does this refer, this note of yours?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. The previous date is the 24th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you tell us what that's all about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am sorry. In relation to what?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Who was -- who was doing the torching that was getting out of hand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it was stated here as an obvious problem that cannot be placed under control. So I do not have a precise answer. The only thing I can say is that it is obvious that this kind of problem was present in that area. Obviously he is stating that with concern, not with support, not supportive of that phenomenon. And in a way he is critical of the local self-government, because otherwise it would not be logical to have any kind of criticism vis-a-vis the local self-government.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. There's a few of them who are talking about this. This says: "Bogi - problems with volunteers - wilfulness."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then another one, the second one also says volunteers?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On torchings that are out of hand?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they're obviously talking about problems in their own area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are these likely to be Albanians who are torching something or is it likely to be someone else? Can you help us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Of course there's no reference to Albanians here. There's no individual reference at all. There is only a reference to perpetrators of such criminal offences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do we know even who was being torched or what was being torched? Whose property or whose persons were the subject of these incidents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, certainly we do know -- or, rather, the person who is reporting about that knows.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, on this page are there statements of individual police officials who are talking about wilfulness, torchings and actually the commission of crimes?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: About that, do you note the title "Keeping up morale"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: These crimes might have been perpetrated by the police officers or volunteers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, certainly suspicions are moving along those lines, too, but I don't think that has anything to do with the other bullet. Perhaps it does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, it's time for the break. We will adjourn for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honours, before Your Honours do, may I raise two very short administrative matters that it may be convenient for the Chamber to decide on before it reconvenes. First, exhibits for this witness, might be it convenient if all parties prepared written submissions? We feel we could provide a tabulated version, I think for both sides' potential witnesses by the end of the week. Would that be a more convenient and better use of time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I am attracted to it. I will discuss that with -- Ms. Higgins?

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Your Honour, in terms of the Prosecution documents that they seek to put in, I'm prepared to deal with them orally. And to make observations on the collection of the documents. So it's in Your Honours' hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll consider that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And the second point, Your Honours, is just, again, we have received a number of inquires from Mr. Kristan, who of course is expecting to be recalled, and is trying to fix his diary, I think, to accommodate us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll consider that too. We are adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic, continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, these two comments that you noted down in your agenda related to the behaviour out of hand. Tell me, how did the officers attending those meetings react to those problems? How did they approach them?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can see, it's quite evident here, that lower-level leaders are pointing out these problems. And it was obviously the position of the leaders in the staff that these problems must be urgently stopped or prevented, and of course the perpetrators of what had already been done must be detected.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Please look now at page 437. You made a note here. I suppose this, too, is your handwriting. It looks like it was written when you were leaning the paper on something unstable. It says: "For discussions with Lazarevic."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Under item 3, it says: "Sanitisation, clearing up the terrain, Dren village - Zubin Potok."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What does it says here?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says: "28 corpses buried without --" I don't know this abbreviation -- "procedure." It should be legal procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It looks to me like "civilian."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's possible. "Civilian" is what it looks like, but it doesn't associate me with the right word to use.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then towards the bottom, it says --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says "Prizren."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Pusto Selo.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Pusto Selo, note submitted to the district public prosecutor." I've already explained this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That's the end of April 1999.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a note to which this aerial photograph was attached.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then on the next page, marked ERN 438, it says: "Aide-memoire for the meeting."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Please try to read this. It's not very legible to me.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is really hard to read.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Under 1, it says --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Aggravated circumstances." And then it says: "They are better organised and more persistent." Next line: "We do not have strong --"

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It says "stronger support."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right. "Stronger support" is what it says. "Airstrikes," and then next line: "Civilians (with them terrorists.)"

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What does it mean, "Civilians," and then "(terrorists with them)"?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We see from the heading "Aggravated Circumstances." It is difficult to resolve problems with terrorists if they are intermingled with civilians. That is something I explained many times, the intermingling of terrorists with civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Why was that an aggravating circumstance, something that made things harder?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It made things harder because the police could not take measures against terrorists if they would endanger thereby the civilians. And I explained several times that in such situations the police refrained to the maximum from taking any repressive measures, although it would have been logical to arrest terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm trying not to ask leading questions, although I understand you very well. Is it the case that the police avoided opening fire if there was a danger of hurting civilians?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is something I said many times, and that is indisputable.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On page ERN number ending with 439, that's the page on which Mr. Nice questioned you, I'm interested only in this one line on which he questioned you quite extensively. It says: "Left the country 900.000." Is it 900.000 or 90.000? Something seems to be crossed out here. Is that what you wrote?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this number doesn't look like it. I never heard the number 900.000. This second 0 is a bit problematic, because it seems to be crossed out. It seems to be 90.000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is it in your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I said several times I'm not saying that this could not be my handwriting, it is, but some details, some letters were shifted or corrected. I said the sequence of the pages is not correct. I said that there's handwriting that isn't mine, such as when the pages are marked, or in several other places, but generally speaking, this is my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... appears to be different from the remaining four, and certainly different --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is different -- I mean, the first and the second 0 are different from the other three. The first is too small, and the second one is too big and has something that looks like a hook that is unintelligible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. But could you tell us with any certainty that you Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. wrote the number 900.000 yourself?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Then at the bottom of this page, it says: "Crime control."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And below that it says: "Residence." What does that refer to?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already explained that this relates to the activity of registering placing of residence of displaced persons in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Then you have ERN number ending with 440. That's the 4th of May, 1999. It says: "Minister," then underneath, "Political part," and then it says, "Return of refugees. Return of the ICRC and the UNHCR." Is that it?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what is it that follows below ICRC and UNHCR?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't read it. The copy is very bad. It looks like "Agreement with Albanians." Maybe "Renewal of negotiations with Albanians."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: No. That doesn't seem to be it. Is it perhaps the agreement about local police?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot identify it unless it is "Renewal of negotiations," meaning political negotiations. I really don't know what it means, what it could mean. Or maybe talks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. On the next page, 441, it says: "President," and then below that, it says: "Crime." I cannot read the other word, but at the bottom it says: "The state must adhere to the law." Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in that last line.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what is this previous line; "Crime," and then I can't make out the following word.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it may be "paramilitaries."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, "Crime, paramilitaries," and then what does it say below?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot identify the little bullet point just underneath.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And how about this sentence: "The state must adhere to the law"? Does that have anything to do with crime or paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Logically so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And on the right page that's yet another meeting of the 5th of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Was that the president's comment, and who was the president?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, I can't tell you with any certainty. I suppose it is the president of the FRY, Slobodan Milosevic, and it would be logical for these to be his points. Or maybe I prepared these points, but I never participated in the discussions at the president's office. I really cannot tell you at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. "Crime, paramilitaries." The next word cannot be made out, but the last line is clear: "The state must adhere to the law."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, do you intend to go through this entire document?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I wish to go through only a few more. I'm skipping entire pages because the entire document shows in a way the continuity of one and the same type of conduct. There is no change of conduct in terms of treatment, legality, multi-ethnic Kosovo, treatment of Albanians, treatment of refugees, et cetera. For instance, 443 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What is the fact that you want or that you are seeking comments from the general on particular items? You could easily just identify those items which you say confirm your proposition that the authorities acted properly and in accordance with law. It's a very tiring exercise and I'm finding it a bit soporific.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honours, it may be -- if I can just interrupt the accused for a second, it may be worth observing that the accused has gone through not just the entries I went through, not related to the purposes that I relied on. I haven't interrupted thus far and don't wish to stop him doing what he's doing, but I shouldn't like the Court to think that the entries that he has turned to, which I didn't deal with at all, are necessarily going to be accepted on the basis that they're now being advanced. I will be simply left in the position of having to deal with them by argument, whereas if they had been raised in chief I would have dealt with them in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The general point that he's seeking to establish was certainly dealt with overall by you in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Absolutely right. But then when it comes to interpretation of particular entries I'm left to argument at the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. What I'm raising with you, Mr. Milosevic, is whether we need to go through the entire document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, bearing in mind the fact that Mr. Nice dealt with this, and he qualified it as a diary, as authentic, and all the rest of it, so in that diary everything that is written I consider to be relevant, because it shows a very continuous, from start to finish, conduct on the part of the police, the behaviour of the police and the conduct of this witness, his attitudes, the positions of his colleagues, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Milosevic. Let us proceed quickly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm trying to get through it as quickly as possible and move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, 443 is the next page, the ERN number. You go on to speak here of your notes, these are your own notes, and instructions which you have for the meetings with the heads of department. Does that coincide with what you said, that pursuant to instructions from the minister, you held meetings with the chiefs?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did attend the meetings but I didn't convene them or preside over them, hold them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. But let's see what the main tasks are. Under number 1, it says reporting residence.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: "Returning weapons, taking charge of populated areas." And number 2, what it says, legality?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Clearing up the terrain, sanitisation, we've already spoken about that. Izbica, criminal offences, isolation, return of weapons, and so on. Urgent end to burning, and that emanates from the previous problems that were highlighted by individual heads of secretariats.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. And what does it say under number 3?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Preventing illegal activities."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: At the very bottom, does it say: "Criminal prosecution"?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it says at the end, but I was reading the two lines above that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Help us clarify what it says at 444, "Meeting with SUP chiefs." And then it goes on to specify the tasks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just before moving off that page, can you help with number 3, which you did speak about, and the reference to the PJP platoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The PJP platoon is mentioned, and I was thinking what that could mean. Perhaps it meant to pinpoint a platoon who -- which would be in charge with preventing illegal activities and not take part in the other assignments. Otherwise, the second point is: "Staff changes, criminal -- criminal persecution," and then in a special point the rest is set out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So 3 is preventing illegal activities.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. And to prevent crime, prevent illegal activities. Possibly it means pinpointing a special unit of the PJP to deal with these issues without taking part in the anti-terrorist activities, just to focus on these issues here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you help also with number 6 and number 7?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, these are units within the PJP. The 88th Detachment of the PJP was a detachment which had certain specials, such as snipers, divers, bellyologists [sic], paratroopers, et cetera. But it was never properly established. And the 122nd Intervention Brigade were two separate detachments of the police, but I don't know what context -- in what context they were placed and why they're included here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, since our attention has been drawn to that, it seems to me that there is quite considerable difference both in the handwriting and in the number 6 introduced here if you compare it to the rest of what it says on page 443.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't pay attention to that, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, that was straightforward leading, really.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not pay attention to that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I think Your Honour's attention was diverted at the time that the accused turned to the question asked by His Honour Judge Bonomy with a leading question about handwriting, and it really invalidates or reduces any value to the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic. The proper course would have been to direct the witness's attention to handwriting and ask him for a comment on both.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that's what I'm asking. I didn't pay attention to that, but when Mr. Bonomy indicated that to me, then this point 6, judging by the handwriting, seems different from the rest of the page, and I've just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, Mr. Milosevic. I told you. I was giving you guidance as to how the question should have been formulated so as not to be leading. You point the witness to both handwritings and then ask him for a comment on them, if he has one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. General, do you have any comment to make? Take a look at this page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: This is -- has he already commented? He hasn't. Okay. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I be allowed to answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't pay attention to that, but now that I see it, point 6, at least the first word I couldn't accept as being written in my own handwriting because obviously it's a different pen, quite obviously the way in which the syllables are written is different, so I would express doubt that point 6 was written by me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What about 7? What about 7?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, 7 seems to be more like my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. But can you remember looking at this note, these notes here, the entry? I know that a lot of time has gone by, but can you remember what this might refer to?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know what it could refer to, but I do know that this detachment with the snipers did exist within the composition of that detachment, but I don't know what it refers to exactly. Whether it means that they should come or whether I should just bear that in mind, take note of that with respect to some other activity training or whatever, I really can't say. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On this page -- rather, page 444, I'm interested in just a few matters. 80B: "We have to restore peace." 80B: "In order to create peace, everybody to do their job, public law and order, security."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: "Serbs do not kill old women and burn --" what does it say here? Burn what? What does it say here?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what it says, more or less, but it's very difficult for me to decipher it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Empty houses?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, "not burn empty houses." So that person who was reading this seemed to understand it better.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that would be consistent with the meaning. "Burn empty houses," I think that that is what it says, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what about the mention of the KLA here? "The KLA has launched an all-out attack." What does that -- and then underneath that there's something in brackets written in very small letters. I can't read it.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't read what it says in brackets either but I can confirm that what you read out does in fact say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And at the bottom, the three lines, I'll do my best to read them: "Somebody used the opportunity to kill and loot," and I can't see what it says after that. Can you?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't read that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What can you read? What can you make out?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when you read it out I can recognise it. I can read this now. "Somebody took advantage of the occasion to --" or "used the opportunity to -- for killing and looting." But after that word, I really can't make anything out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, on the next page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I'd like to hear the comments on that passage. Somebody taking the opportunity to kill somebody, what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I can't say. I'm giving thought to the entire context in which this is written, this sentence is written, and trying to make out what that meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It says here: "Somebody took the opportunity to commit murder, or to kill and loot, and they --"

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember thinking that thought.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then it's very legible on the next side, if it is the following page of that same agenda, very nicely, neatly written and quite different from the previous writing, it says: "Violence was made impossible, prevented." That's at the end of the sentence. Is this your handwriting? Can you read it, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think it is my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What does it say, then?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps it says: "Energetic action on the part of the police has prevented violence."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. "Energetic work by the police has prevented violence."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And under number 2: "Putting the Albanian population in order."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Of the Albanians is being organised." "Boraviste," "residence." Clearing up the terrain or sanitisation. Hand-over and take-over of villages. It probably has to do with the activity related to putting order into the Albanian population with respect to recording their residence, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what about sanitisation or clearing the terrain?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably in the sense that where the army and police leaves, that the population, that the citizens can come back straight away, and the hand-over and take-over, we know that means, so there are no complaints along those lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, at the bottom, it says: "There are no private wars." What does that refer to?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it means to prevent voluntariness and self-will and anarchy of all types linked to crimes, criminal offences, and that kind of thing, because it was considered that individuals, volunteers were engaging in their own private wars and that that had to be prevented and that any such behaviour should be dealt with.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, 446 page there. Mr. Nice asked you a number of things. 172246 is the ERN number, 446 being the last digits. I think it says here that it's page 82, but you say that that is not your pagination in the -- 446 is the typed out ERN number. It's on the next page. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, what did you say with respect to page 82?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was saying it's 82 that I have, but that is not my writing, so I didn't write that number 82 for the page number there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Right. Fine. Now, Mr. Nice, yesterday especially asked you something to do with what it says here on the left-hand side under 1, dealing with the area, then recording of residence and weapons and everything else from the UP [phoen] it says in the B/C/S. What does that refer to?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the decree or provision governing the recording of residence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Right. Now something that Mr. Nice asked you, I don't know whether it was anybody else from the Trial Chamber, the asanacija, sanitisation or clearing up of the terrain. And then underneath, what does it say? "We must know the truth," is that what it says? "We must know the truth."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "Each case must be solved Izbica - Buha." That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: "Izbica - Buha," does that mean that he is put in charge of investigating the matter or what? In the context, what would you say in this context?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That means, as I explained it yesterday, that Buha should undertake all steps to establish what happened there and whether what we heard about had actually happened, that he should take part in establishing the facts of what happened in Izbica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Then Mr. Nice went on to ask you this: He asked you about a list that he provided yesterday in English. It says: "Schedule F, Persons known by name killed at Izbica [In English] 28 March 1999." [Interpretation] And then we saw there that a certain number of those individuals were to be found or had been found, or it is stated that they were found in Serbia. Tell me now, please, General, all this business around clearing up the terrain in Izbica, was that conducted in such a way as to enable everybody to be identified and that exhumation take place, photographing take place, and all the rest of it?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I explained all that. In these exhibits here, we find documents which relate to this entire case, including photographs taken of all the victims found in that grave site, and there are also sketches and diagrams of the persons individually buried in several cemeteries in that region.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, take a look, please, at this whole binder. I don't know what number it is, what binder it is. I've made a note of it here, but I can't read -- I think it says 11, binder 11. But the whole binder is one tab, and it is tab 418. A single binder for a single tab. The whole binder is a single tab, 418. It's Izbica. Yesterday, Mr. Nice claimed that this was done with some kind of excavator in order to destroy the corpses. Does this entire binder contain photographs of all of those who were taken out, and can it be established on any photograph that the corpses were destroyed in this way?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. These are photographs of all the corpses found at the cemetery in Izbica. They were photographed there from number 1 to number 101. Sometimes one, sometimes two, sometimes even four photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right, General. If all these measures were taken, then, as instructed, and it can be seen throughout this binder how the police worked and how the police forensic experts worked - let this not be a leading question - how can this be linked up with the efforts made by the police in general with regard to such measures?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained that in this case the police worked, to the best of my knowledge, completely in accordance with the law. Of course, the military organs in charge also took part in some of these measures, including forensic experts, forensic doctors from the Military Medical Academy. Yesterday I did not see any trace of any excavator on these photographs, and I don't know any details about this, but I don't know whether it's possible at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. What was done here, it's not one single measure that was taken but 101 measures, as you said. 101 bodies were photographed. Can this be linked up in any way to the intention of any level of government to conceal anything that was done? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This absolutely cannot be done -- cannot be linked up with any intention to conceal anything. Finding any of these bodies outside the grave or cemetery where they were buried is totally illogical, as far as I'm concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You were asked a question earlier and I'm not certain whether it was answered, which is: "Can it be established on any photograph that the corpses were destroyed in this way?" A reference to the excavator being used to disinter the bodies. And then the answer which comes below is, "Yes, I remember." So I'm not sure what that "yes" means.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure even now, but it's quite certain that all the photographs that I saw - of course I'm not an expert - but there's not a single element that could lead me to believe that this was done in the way that the Prosecutor explained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is there a record of where the bodies were re-interred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. In these documents here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you direct our attention to that, then, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've found it. I need just a moment to find my way.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bonomy, it's all of binder number 10. It pertains to Izbica and the documents. 11 contains only photographs.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tab 412 gives the report of the scene and also the burial of the bodies. And also, there's a sketch with photographs. I think that the documentation on these same questions pertains to documents through tab 417.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So can you point me to a page where it tells us how a body or any number of bodies were re-interred?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bonomy, in tab 412 there is the interment of 15 persons, and in 413 a report on the burial of 20 persons, then in number 14 about the burial of yet another number. Every time records were made; 15, 25, and 16.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But it's not just one page. Are these -- are these tabs translated? The first page in each one seems to be, but are the other pages translated?

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: The other pages appear, Your Honour, to be photographs. There's a first page translation of the report face, followed by photographs of burial sites, it appears.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but on the next page there is always a sketch of the scene, and then in tab 412 we can see a sketch of the scene, the Muslim city cemetery, the Municipal Assembly of Kosovska Mitrovica, and then you can see the stamp of the Ministry of the Interior on the top, and also a sketch where who was, and their names too, names of the interred persons. I don't know if you can see that in tab 412. The heading is "Sketch of the scene, Muslim city cemetery." The date is the 4th of May -- no. I can't see this. Is it May or is it June? It seems to be the fifth month. That is May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The 4th of June is the date, but what I would like to hear from the witness is what this document tells us, what he understands it to say.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you mean tab 412 and the tabs that follow?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: 412 as an example. What does that actually tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a document of the criminal technical department of the SUP in Kosovska Mitrovica that says where the bodies found in Izbica were buried, and this was done on orders from the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, that says: "Burial of 15 bodies"; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And you say that the plan then tells us where the 15 bodies were buried.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, which document tells us about the -- when they were first exhumed? Which body tells us about that -- which document, rather, tells us about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is a document that speaks of that, too, but I have to find it somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, I can't find my way that quickly, but is that tab 410 where it says: "Report on finding a body, a corpse. Total 101." Same binder. Then there is a sketch of the cemetery in Izbica where they were found. In 409 there's a list from 1 to 101, and 410 there is a report.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 410 is individual reports on each individual corpse that had been found, while tab 407 should speak of this, although I'm not quite sure at this very moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, can you remind me what evidence is there -- direct evidence, I don't mean evidence of where bodies may have been found, but is there any direct evidence relating to subsequent events at this cemetery?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm not aware at the moment - that doesn't mean to say it doesn't exist - of any evidence dealing directly with this cemetery. I'm just confirming the source of our material for the material we put on the map and in the chart that suggested a distribution of bodies in various local cemeteries as well as elsewhere, and indeed was going to make the point that the Prosecution doesn't necessarily challenge the interment of bodies in these subsequent cemeteries, although it's more interested in the ones in Serbia. The evidence of what happened at the original disinterment came from the witnesses who saw that happening, and that's where we got the evidence of the use of an excavator, not of course for the purposes of destruction but for the purposes of -- absolutely not destruction, for the purposes of removal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: These documents we're looking at at the moment indicate that 101 bodies were buried in various cemeteries, is that right, locally?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But your records indicate that some of these bodies have been found elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Correct. And we haven't yet done or been able to do a complete reconciliation between these documents and any other materials that we have, but -- and some of this material, as the Court may remember, has only come in since the close of the Prosecution's case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That clarifies the state of the evidence, which is what I wanted to know. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right, General. There are sketches of where they were found here and documents about each individually exhumed and examined body and then documents containing diagrams where everybody was buried.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, since all of this is so well documented, in whose interest would it be to disinter someone and then re-inter them in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I tried to explain this as a mystery. I really have no explanation for this. Who would do such a thing, namely to disinter persons who had already been buried and where post-mortems were carried out, why they would be disinterred and taken 400 kilometres away from that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the news on this transfer of bodies appeared once I was already in prison?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that. I found out from the media.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In the indictment it says that survivors testified as to what had happened or, rather, Mr. Nice claims that survivors testified about what had happened, and in the indictment it says that survivors had been deported. Did you have the opportunity of reading that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Then I'm not going to ask you about that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At any rate, Mr. Robinson, both cannot be the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: General, do you happen to have that page of your agenda still? Page 82 of your handwriting.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The last three lines of bullet point 2, titled "Crime prevention," says like this -- did you find it? "Masks/kill," and with a -- back again: "There can be no private wars. The responsibility for civil conflict must not fall on the police." Could you clarify the meaning of these passages? I'm interested in particular "Masks/kill."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's as if I saw this for the first time. It says: "Deprive of life."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what is between "mask" and "deprive"?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's sort of a slanted line. Absolutely I cannot give an answer. I do not remember having jotted this down, or I have no idea what this would refer to. As if somebody who was wearing masks, should be deprived of life? But this is an impossible formulation. And it looks as if this were added on in some kind of small lettering, although I could say this was my handwriting. Really, it is quite legible, just as you read it. It does not say "kill," it says "deprive of life."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You gave some explanation as to the meaning of private wars to my previous question. Given that, can I take it that some volunteers with masks took the advantage of that chaotic situation to -- to do something bad?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that is one of the possible theses, but even if that were the case, I certainly would not have written down "deprive of life," even in such a case. I'm sure of that. And I do not recall that we had any persons with masks. Absolutely not. Some parts of uniform were not worn properly, and then there were different bandannas and whatever, and that was something that was opposed, but I don't remember anyone operating in Kosovo with masks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'd like to ask the parties a question. It has been occurring to me what -- what weight is to be given to the diary or agenda and the questions and answers on it? Because so much of it appears to be guesswork, and because a lot of it is not legible. So in determining what weight should be attached to it, Ms. Higgins, what would your submission be?

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Ultimately, Your Honour, I can only say that the document has to be viewed in its entirety. Evidently someone from the translation unit has been through the document and been able to tie up an English version, which the witness has also been able to assist with. And the Trial Chamber ultimately will have to view in its totality the evidence that has been given from the witness, and as Your Honour observes, some of that is general and the Chamber in due course will have to deal with the generality. Some of it has been specific. I'm afraid it's one of those occasions where the weight will be determined by the totality of the evidence in the round. I'm not sure I can assist further than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Milosevic, how should the Trial Chamber approach the question of the weight to be attached to the diary in light of all the circumstances?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I think the logical answer, Mr. Robinson, is, since we are talking about personal working notes, that we look at what the witness says about them. I think that is the most relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm asking the question because so much of it can't be -- is not legible. And then you ask a question, and he -- he surmises. He makes a conjecture as to what he thinks it says and what it means. That's the difficulty I'm having with it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
