utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, maybe that is true of some individual words, but I thought that those parts that the witness was able to read was indubitably legible. I'm not, of course, as able to read his handwriting as he is himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, you have a point there. In respect of those parts where the writing is legible and he can read it, and it is his writing, then he can say what it means. Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The interest which I took in cross-examination were entries he always acknowledged were in his hand. Those entries can be considered individually as supportive of various aspects of the Prosecution's case. There is, of course, one issue of interpretation in respect of "back-breaking" or "perfidious" which has yet to be dealt with. In fact, it's not an easy problem, but that apart, they were all quite clear. That's the value I place on the document. There are other entries that I might have turned to, with unlimited time, but didn't, and I will refer to those in argument. As to the generality of the document, the accused is entitled to seek the benefit of the document if he can find in other entries matters to assist him. They haven't been cross-examined on by me but I've made that point already. So our submission is individual entries can be considered in isolation certainly where the handwriting is clear, and that's the way I've cross-examined. While I'm on my feet, just to amplify my answer to His Honour Judge Bonomy, one witness who deals quite comprehensively with this matter is Draga, and although we may not have done a reconciliation of bodies in the various grave sites that have -- are referred to, the process of identification followed exhumation by UNMIK and by Serbia and reflects death certificates issued following those exhumations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: As for translation issue, you don't have a position against -- the same page, "remove traces of violence against civilians," which was corrected as "property."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: No, I don't have -- as far as I know, we have no point on that one. It's only the other one which we're waiting for the report from CLSS, and in any event there are other issues that I may have to touch on in other evidence -- with other evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's time for the adjournment. Before we adjourn, I should say that -- just let me finish. On the first point raised by Mr. Nice, Ms. Higgins, although we would very much like to hear you in Court, we are going to require that submissions be put in writing in relation to the question of the admissibility of the various documents.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, regarding your question, namely to what extent this can be used as evidence, I believe that the answer is that to the extent to which certain things are repeated very clearly on many occasions in the agenda, consistent protection of refugees, consistent treatment and attitude to certain issues, the conduct of the police as directed by general policy and things that can be followed very clearly from this text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic. You say they establish a culture of propriety, proper conduct. I understand the submission. With regard to the other point raised by Mr. Nice, that's the witness Ivan Kristan, we'll give a decision on that tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So submissions in writing for the admission of the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And we'll prepare both submissions in tabular form to assist. It may be, if we get them done in time, that the parties can use them electronically but if you want them by the end of the week they may have to prepare their own because we may not have got it done in time for them to use our tabular form.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, I kindly ask you not to require from me to provide any other documents or arguments than are presented here. I have provided a huge volume, 17 binders including more than 500 exhibits, plus questioning of witness on those exhibits. I don't know what other arguments I am supposed to present for the admission of those exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think the Chamber has decided to utilise the procedure suggested by Mr. Nice because it has obvious advantages. I think were we to have an oral hearing, it would take a very long time, Mr. Milosevic. You have associates. You have the assigned counsel. So get to work. We are adjourned until tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 8th day of June, 2005, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25
